title: Longest Chain by Adding a Letter
statement:
You get a list of distinct lowercase words. Word x can step to word y if you can get y by inserting exactly one letter, anywhere, into x, without reordering the other letters. So "at" steps to "cat", "art" and "ate", but not to "tab".

A chain is a sequence of words from the list where each word steps to the next. Return the length of the longest chain. A single word is a chain of length 1. The words may be used in any order, not the order they are given.

examples.why: k → ka → kat → kart. The r goes into the middle, which is allowed. "cart" only follows "art" or "car", and "car" is missing.
xy → xzy works. yxz has the right letters, but x and y are in the wrong order, so it is not reachable.
o → on → one → bone → bonet. The list is shuffled, so you must not rely on the given order.

constraints: words are distinct and contain only lowercase letters
hints: A chain only ever gets longer by one letter per step. In which order should you process the words so that every word's predecessors are handled before it?
Sort by length. Then the best chain ending at a word is 1 plus the best chain ending at any word that steps to it.
Instead of testing every shorter word, generate the predecessors: delete each letter of the word in turn and look the result up in a map of best chain lengths.

explain.intuition:
Let best[w] be the longest chain that ends at word w. The word before w in that chain is one letter shorter, so if words are processed from shortest to longest, every possible predecessor already has its answer.

The step that makes it fast: a word of length L has at most L predecessors, and you can list them by deleting one letter at a time. Looking each one up in a hash map costs about O(L), so you never compare pairs of words. Deleting is easier than inserting, since inserting would mean trying 26 letters at L + 1 positions.
steps: For each position i, form w without its i-th letter. If that word is in best, set best[w] = max(best[w], best[prev] + 1).
pitfalls: Processing the words in the given order. A predecessor that appears later in the list has no answer yet.
Treating the step as "same letters plus one" and ignoring order. xy does not step to yxz.
Counting edges instead of words. A chain of a single word has length 1, not 0.

solutions.title: Compare every pair
solutions.idea: Sort by length. For each pair whose lengths differ by one, check with two pointers whether the shorter one steps to the longer one.

solutions.title: Delete one letter and look it up
solutions.idea: Sort by length, then for each word try every one-letter deletion and look it up in a map of best chain lengths so far.

followups: Return the chain itself, not only its length.
Allow a step to insert or delete a letter, so chains can go both ways. What does the problem become?
